correctness.rationale: The outer bands agree and are forward invariant; the central bands exchange, with both squares f on K and rfr on R. The odd orbit points differ by a shifted f-sequence, leaving precisely one signed pair of atoms in the empirical-measure difference. Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality then gives the atom displacement divided by n. The 3^m full affine branches of the iterate have equal lengths, so extremal displacement is maximized at a mesh vertex and the first non-endpoint vertex realizes 1/4−3^(−m)/4; m=0 gives zero. Integrating uniform orbit-sum discrepancy against an invariant law, then applying the pushforward and taking the Cesàro limit, identifies both invariant simplices. Entropy of the common square gives equality of individual measure entropies and hence of all the variational pressure and maximizing sets. The three equal-magnitude branches preserve normalized Lebesgue on K, and reflection exchanges the halves. In centered coordinates around 1/2 write the even/odd parts of q as A+Cz² and Bz+Dz³, where C=a2+3a3/2 and D=a3. In the lag-one difference the terms other than CD cancel by reflection about the midpoint of K and the equidistribution of y and f(y). For d=1/8, standardized coordinates h=(y−3/8)/d and H=(f(y)−3/8)/d, the remaining term is −2d^5 CD E[h³H−hH³]. Exact integration gives E[h³H−hH³]=32/405, producing the stated coefficient and cubic witness. The maps are nonconjugate: an endpoint-reversing conjugacy is excluded by A(1)=0 and B(0)=3/4; an increasing one must map the second turning point to the second, forcing the fixed point 1/2 to map to the nonfixed point 1/4. The period-orbit sets also agree: central periodic orbits other than the shared midpoint have even periods and the shifted odd sequences have the same underlying atoms.
